title: FaaSMem: Improving Memory Efficiency of Serverless Computing with Memory Pool Architecture
problem: Idle containers in serverless computing continue to occupy memory to avoid cold startup penalties, wasting memory resources. Existing memory offloading policies either compromise Quality of Service or operate at granularities too coarse for serverless scenarios.
motivation: Memory is a scarce resource in data centers, and improving its efficiency in serverless environments is critical for reducing infrastructure costs and enabling better resource utilization.
method: FaaSMem works by moving unused memory from idle serverless containers to a shared remote pool (network storage) instead of keeping it all locally. Rather than moving memory in large blocks—which would slow down applications—it uses fine-grained offloading policies (precise rules about which data to move and when). This lets the system recover wasted memory from idle containers while keeping response times fast.
key_novelty: The core innovation is using a remote memory pool with fine-grained offloading policies specifically for serverless computing, enabling memory recovery without sacrificing application response times.
contributions: Identifies memory waste problem in idle serverless containers and quantifies its impact on data center efficiency
Proposes FaaSMem system with memory pool architecture for transparent memory offloading
Develops fine-grained offloading policies that maintain QoS while improving memory efficiency
Demonstrates practical improvements in memory utilization for serverless workloads
limitations: Limitations and overhead of remote memory access are not discussed in the abstract.
